title: HiPER: Hierarchically-Composed Processing for Efficient Robot Learning-Based Control
problem: Learning-Based Model Predictive Control (LMPC) for robot navigation combines neural network inference with iterative MPC optimization, creating a mixed workload with rapidly varying computational patterns that neither GPUs nor simple CPU-GPU integrations can serve efficiently. The workload alternates between dense ML computation and sparse, irregular MPC solves across time steps.
motivation: Robotic autonomy increasingly demands real-time LMPC at the edge, but the unique temporal and spatial variability of LMPC workloads exceeds the adaptability of general-purpose GPU architectures.
method: HiPER is a 1024-PE ASIC synthesized in 16nm CMOS (16.37 mm²) built around a fractal interconnect topology that nests local systolic arrays within a hierarchical extension to handle the traffic characteristics of LMPC. A six-level pointer queue hierarchy orchestrates program composition and execution, enabling temporal and spatial mapping of workload phases at runtime. The pointer queues serve as a lightweight control mechanism that composes heterogeneous sub-programs without a complex scheduler, allowing dynamic adaptation to workload changes.
key_novelty: Fractal interconnect topology combining local systolic arrays with hierarchical extensions, orchestrated by a multi-level pointer queue hierarchy that enables runtime temporal and spatial remapping for mixed ML+MPC workloads.
contributions: Hierarchically-composed processing array with fractal systolic interconnect supporting both dense ML and irregular MPC computation.
Six-level pointer queue control hierarchy enabling lightweight runtime workload composition and adaptation.
10.75x performance improvement over GTX 1080 GPU and 12.80x energy efficiency improvement over Jetson Orin Nano.
11.6x/22.2x performance improvement over RoboX/Plasticine accelerators for LMPC workloads.

metrics.speedup: 10.75x over GTX 1080; 11.6x over RoboX; 22.2x over Plasticine
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 12.80x energy efficiency improvement over Jetson Orin Nano

limitations: Evaluation targets a single representative LMPC workload; generalization to diverse robot tasks or other mixed ML+solver applications is not demonstrated.
primary_theme: ASIC accelerator for robot learning-based model predictive control
